elements.text: Your first generator. It burns any fuel; a coal block burns longer and gives more. It pushes power out on every side by itself, so put machines and cables right next to it.
They run on their own as long as they see open sky. Full output by day, a quarter at night.
There are ten tiers and each is far stronger than the last. The first is made of silicon, and the tenth, the Dyson panel, is the most powerful generator in the mod.
Instead of laying out a field of panels, put them in the **combiner**: it holds up to 18 panels and outputs their combined power from one block. The combiner itself must see the sky.

You build the wind turbine yourself, bottom to top: a **base**, 2 to 10 **mast sections** on it, the **nacelle** on the top section and a **rotor** in the nacelle: right-click it with the rotor. It runs day and night without fuel and gives power out of the base on every side but the top.

The taller the mast, the more it makes: 2 sections give half, 10 sections give it all. A high site helps too, a turbine on a mountain beats one by the sea. Rain gives half as much again, a thunderstorm doubles it. The wind keeps changing and the nacelle turns after it, so put an energy bank next to it.

The rotor needs room: open sky above the nacelle and 5×5 of free space around it. To take the rotor out, sneak and right-click with an empty hand. Turbines closer than 6 blocks take wind from each other. Click any part with an empty hand to see the output, or what holds it back, above the hotbar.

Cables carry power from generators to machines. Each one has a limit on how much it passes per tick. In order: copper, ferro, gold, crystalline, emerald, heavy, and netherite fiber, which has almost no limit.
The bare wire for the energy magistral only comes from **wire cutters**, out of a redstone block.

You can hide a cable or a heat pipe inside any full block, like stone or planks, and it keeps working as before. Hold the block, sneak and right-click the cable. To take the cover off, sneak and right-click with the wrench: the first click removes the cover, the next one the cable itself.

They store power and go into crafting: the **charging amulet**, the **charging packs** and other powered gear are built from them. They don't charge anything by themselves. To top up your tools on the go, carry a charging amulet or pack. From smallest to largest: battery, lithium battery, flux core and plasma core.
A big 10M FE battery block. In its window you set how many percent to keep in reserve, and everything above that goes back into the grid. It also shows how much power comes in and out.

The bank keeps its charge: pick it up with a wrench or a pickaxe and the energy stays inside. Higher tiers hold more and move it faster. **T2** is crafted from a T1 on a crafting table and takes over its charge. **T3** comes out of the industrial assembler empty, so drain the T2 first.
Put a battery, cell or tool inside, run a cable to it, and it charges the item from the grid.

Run a cable to the plate and stand on it: everything you carry gets charged. Armour and backpack first, then your hands, then the whole inventory. No need to take your suit off and carry things to a charger. The field and the posts glow while it works.
